_meta.description: The messaging service account's grant (ADR-037 fragment). The SMS and WhatsApp provider webhooks are PublicPages, so OpenRegister sees Anonymous. After a callback's signature checks out, the webhook writes as one Nextcloud account an admin picks (MessagingServiceAccount), with OpenRegister's checks on. These are the schemas a webhook writes: channelMessage (the inbound message), channelConversation (opened and touched for a known contact), ticket (the contact moment for a message from an unknown number) and messagingConsentRecord (a STOP or opt-in, only while consent is not yet in integriq). Each grants pipelinq-messaging-service create and update. They keep 'authenticated' on every action: agents read and answer conversations and log contact moments as themselves, which the open default allowed before, so the block changes nothing for a logged-in user and only names what the webhook account may do. Admins keep OpenRegister's admin bypass. Lookups (provider, contact, conversation) stay reads without RBAC. The repair step CreateMessagingServiceGroup creates the group.
